To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the temperature in the tip is a function of the initial green density, that the maximum temperature is reached at the tip and that the temperature distribution across a powder compact depends on the green density.

(a) the maximum temperature in a CATS experiment is not only a function of the applied current but also of the initial green density, and (b) the temperature distribution across a powder compact is not only a consequence of the applied current and the initial green density but also of the effective current density.
the maximum temperature and the temperature gradient in the tip during CATS are strongly dependent on the initial green density of the powder compact.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new sintering technique for the fabrication of dense, high quality metal parts.
the development and application of novel techniques to study the temperature distribution in the tip and powder compacts during CATS.
the understanding of the thermal and electrical phenomena in CATS and the effects of these phenomena on the densification of nickel powder compaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
densification of the powder compact in CATS is a complex function of the current density and the green density of the powder compact.
a high green density is beneficial to the densification of the powder compact, but not to the temperature distribution in the tip or the powder compact.
the temperature in the tip is a function of the current, the green density, the contact area between the tip and the compact and the thermal conductivity of the material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temperature evolution during CATS of nickel can be controlled and optimized by varying the green compact density.
the current distribution is the key parameter in determining the temperature distribution and the resulting densification in the powder compact.
the densification parameter is not only a function of the current and time, but also a function of the initial green density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CATS process can be used to locally sinter powder compacts with a high degree of control over the temperature and density of the final sintered body.
the current and temperature distributions can be manipulated to control the sintering behavior of a powder compact.
the temperature evolution in the powder bed and tip during CATS can be controlled by varying the green density of the compact.
